answer: Because the opal index resolves every citation against the juniper checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the oasis audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 46 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 46 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 7 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
